author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Florida Atlantic baseball ends season with 3-2 loss to Wichita State
text:
Florida Atlantic baseball was eliminated from the American Conference Tournament after a 3-2 defeat to Wichita State in a play-in game on May 20. The loss brought the Owls’ season to an end, while Wichita State advanced to face Rice in the next round of the tournament.
The matchup was marked by strong pitching from both teams. Florida Atlantic starter James Litman struck out six batters over the first four innings and finished with seven strikeouts in 4.2 innings, allowing only one run on two hits. The Owls took an early lead in the second inning with a sacrifice fly by Brando Leroux after reaching base through a hit and two hit batters.
Wichita State tied the game in the fifth inning, prompting Florida Atlantic to bring Kide Adetuyi onto the mound for relief. In the sixth inning, John Martinez gave FAU a brief lead with a solo home run, but that advantage held only until late in the game.
The turning point came in the top of the ninth when FAU outfielder Kyle Boylston lost sight of a pop-up due to sun glare, putting Wichita State’s tying run at second base. The Shockers capitalized with two singles—one tying and another giving them their final lead at 3-2.
Despite drawing a two-out walk in their last opportunity at bat, Florida Atlantic could not rally back. Offensively, FAU managed just three hits: singles from Nick Romano and Brett Patten along with Martinez’s home run. Adetuyi pitched effectively for 4.1 innings of relief with three strikeouts and one walk.
